podcast.title: Creative Differences with Management
podcast.body: Brian Dorody, a holdover from Big Wreck, was initially excluded from the Thorneley lineup because management felt his presence would make the new band too similar to Big Wreck, aiming for Thorneley to be a "separate sort of thing." This decision added strain to relationships. "Brian was initially going to be the other guitar player in Thorneley. And then the sort of what's called the grown-ups, the people on the other side of the desk, where like, it's too much like Big Rec of Brian's around."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation of the Band
podcast.body: After the first Big Wreck disbanded, Ian Thorneley moved to Toronto, got married, and began writing, leading to the formation of the band "Thorneley." The lineup, except for Brian Dorody, was new. "His relationship with Chad Kruger of Nickelback led him deciding with 604 Records out of Vancouver. And this was the beginning of a brand new band simply called Thorneley..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ken Tizzard's Collaboration
podcast.body: Ken Tizzard, formerly the bassist for The Watchmen, collaborated with Ian Thornley's band for a period, showcasing professional connections among Canadian musicians. "Baseplayer Ken Tizzard worked with Ian Thornley's band for a while."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Touring and Lineup Changes
podcast.body: The band Thorneley engaged in tours, including one where guitarist Paula announced she would be absent for a gig in Edmonton due to her honeymoon. This unexpected vacancy led to Brian Dorody filling in, which subsequently contributed to the reformation of Big Wreck. "Paula was like, oh, by the way, that gig in Edmonton, I'm not going to be there. As I'm going on my honeymoon in Portugal..."

xref.title: Berklee College of Music Admission
xref.body: Ian Thornley was admitted to the Berklee School of Music in Boston after submitting a 4-track demo featuring his compositions and various instrumental parts. His prior musical training, including piano studies with jazz musician Darwin Grosse, contributed to his foundational understanding of harmony and theory, which likely aided his admission. "I just, I had put together, you know, I had a little foretrack thing and I had written a bunch of compositions and, and don't know all these parts, put them all together and just sent those down."

xref.title: Cabbagetown Gig Experience
xref.body: As a 13-year-old, Ian Thornley filled in as a keyboard player for a band with a singer named Chrissy (a cousin). The band needed a replacement keyboardist for a gig at the Cabbagetown band after their previous player bailed. Despite his young age, he looked the part and managed to play the "pretty straightforward music" effectively. "I used an ironing board as a keyboard stand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Childhood Friend of Brian Doherty
xref.body: Dave Henning grew up with Brian Doherty in New York and roomed with him at Berklee School of Music, next door to Ian Thornley. He was an "obvious choice" for the bassist position in Big Wreck due to his existing connection with Brian. "Dave Hending was the obvious choice because he was, you know, grew up with Brian."

xref.title: Cousin of Ian Thornley
xref.body: Chrissy was the singer in an early pop band with Ian Thornley, described as his "cousin twice removed." She helped Ian get a gig with the band after their keyboard player bailed. "a cousin twice removed or something was the singer, Chrissy."

xref.title: Early Bandmate with Ian Thornley
xref.body: Kurt Schaffer was a guitarist in an early pop band with a 13-year-old Ian Thornley. Schaffer was 21 at the time and was the next youngest member of the band. He later gained recognition for playing with Alannah Myles, including on her hit "Black Velvet." "I was in a band with Kurt Schafter. He was the next young guy."

xref.title: Early Electric Guitar Influences
xref.body: Ian Thornley quickly acquired an electric guitar, a delay pedal, and a whammy bar, eager to emulate his influences. He was particularly obsessed with Bruce Cockburn's song "If a Tree Falls" and also practiced U2's music, using the gear to achieve similar sounds. "I was obsessed with if a tree falls or, yeah, if a tree falls. And that that, he used the whammy bar and the delay pedal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Musical Obsession
xref.body: Ian Thornley became obsessed with music from a very young age, starting around four or five years old. He began his musical journey on piano after a family friend had one, showing him a few things that he quickly picked up. His mother, who was also very musical and wanted to learn piano, decided they would both take lessons together around the age of five. "I've been obsessed with music from a very young age, from about four or five."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Engineer for Big Wreck Demos
xref.body: Matti Mateo was the engineer at Presence studio who worked with Big Wreck on their early demos. Ian Thornley and the band "really got on with him" during the recording sessions. "particularly the engineer who was Matti Mateo and really got on with him."

xref.title: Formation in Boston
xref.body: Big Wreck was formed in Boston, Massachusetts, out of collaborations between Ian Thornley, Brian Doherty, Dave Henning, and Forest Williams, who had met while attending Berklee School of Music. "It was formed in Boston."

xref.title: Front of House Mixer
xref.body: Mark Fraccard, a friend and collaborator of Ian Thornley, served as the front of house mixer for The Tragically Hip. "Mark Freakon. He was the front house mixer for the hip."

xref.title: Ken Tizzard's Post-Band Career
xref.body: Bass player Ken Tizzard worked with Ian Thornley's band for a period before embarking on a solo career, releasing two solo albums, one of which came out in 2018. This demonstrates his continued dedication to music as an independent artist. "Baseplayer Ken Tizzard worked with Ian Thornley's band for a while before releasing a couple of Sola Welvens, one came out in 2018."

xref.title: Management Trust Member
xref.body: Alan Gregg was part of The Management Trust, Big Wreck's management company. He was instrumental in helping Ian Thornley regain entry to the US after his student visa expired, facilitating the reunion of the band. "It was Alan Greg and Alan was like, well, yeah, you know, he knows people. So he called people, got me back down there and put the band through the ringer."

xref.title: Met Ian Thornley at Berklee
xref.body: Brian Doherty, a drummer, met Ian Thornley during his second semester at Berklee School of Music. They became fast friends and shared an apartment in Roxbury, where they began formulating ideas for a band. "Brian and I had met, it was in Brian Dirty. Yeah. We had met first, first year, second semester."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Met Ian Thornley at Berklee
xref.body: Forest Williams, the bassist for Big Wreck, met Ian Thornley on the third floor of their dorms at Berklee School of Music. "I had already met Forest, and I was on the third floor."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Piano Teacher to Young Ian Thornley
xref.body: Darwin Grosse, a "heavy jazz guy," taught piano to Ian Thornley when Ian was very young, despite Grosse not typically teaching children. This early instruction provided Ian with a foundational understanding of harmony and theory. "I studied with, I'd studied piano at one point with Darwin Acid, who didn't even teach kids back when I was really little."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Search for a Singer
xref.body: Initially, Big Wreck struggled to find a suitable singer, leading to Ian Thornley reluctantly taking on the vocal duties himself. They even tried out one singer who turned out to be associated with a "gang" and was suspected of stealing from the band's van, leading to his swift dismissal. "How did you end up singing? Because we couldn't find one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Velvet Revolver Audition
xref.body: Ian Thornley was offered the opportunity to become the lead singer and frontman for Velvet Revolver on two separate occasions. "he was offered the opportunity to become the lead singer in frontman for Velvet Revolver."
